title: When I Heard the Learn’d Astronomer
author: Walt Whitman
intro: How much of what we learn adequately explains the world around us? Read the poem “When I Heard the Learn’d Astronomer” to learn what the poet has to say about this question. Answer the questions that follow.
lines: When I heard the learn’d astronomer,
When the proofs, the figures, were ranged in columns before me,
When I was shown the charts and diagrams, to add, divide, and measure them,
When I, sitting, heard the astronomer where he lectured with much applause in the lecture room,
How soon unaccountable I became tired and sick,
Till rising and gliding out I wander’d off by myself,
In the mystical* moist night air, and from time to time,
Look’d up in perfect silence at the stars.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements represents the main theme of the poem?

choices.A: Science cannot fully express the wonder of the world.
choices.B: Nature is one’s best source of recreation.
choices.C: Technology causes more problems than it solves.
choices.D: Learning causes one to become ill and fatigued.

questions.stem: In line 5, what is conveyed by the phrase “tired and sick”?

choices.A: the speaker’s sorrow and loss experienced in his life
choices.C: a sense of the speaker’s poor health
choices.D: the speaker’s boredom and disappointment with the lecture

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the phrase “perfect silence” in the last line of the poem?

choices.A: to explain why he has to leave the lecture room
choices.B: to convey a sense of loneliness and sorrow
choices.C: to contrast with the sounds in the lecture room
choices.D: to highlight the pleasure of science and learning

questions.stem: What do the last three lines of the poem suggest?

choices.A: the importance of personal experience with nature
choices.B: the dangers of losing track of time
choices.C: the importance of learning about astronomy
choices.D: the dangers of wandering off alone
